thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1 triggered — upstream transit provider (AS64500) high packet loss + BGP flaps observed, affecting egress from us-east-1. INC-20231205-17. Auto-page sent to oncall.

pagerduty-bot: @dave (oncall) — pagerduty: P1: Upstream transit packet loss — 50%+ loss on some paths.

dave (oncall): Ack. Investigating. Which regions / services reported?

anna (support): Seeing increased 5xx for hosted API endpoints in us-east-1: customer reports and synthetic checks alerting since ~06:00 UTC. A few Dedicated customers in us-east experiencing elevated request latencies and timeouts.

owen (netops): I can see BGP session flaps toward AS64500 on our edge routers. Intermittent withdraws for a few /21s that we carry. Packet loss spikes on paths that transit AS64500. Running quick checks now.

sam: Traceroute from egress host to 8.8.8.8:
```
traceroute to 8.8.8.8 (8.8.8.8), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.1.1  0.4 ms
 2  198.51.100.1  1.1 ms AS64500
 3  * * *
```
Looks like packet loss after the peer hop.

maya: Confirmed with mtr from a couple of regions — high loss right after peer. Also seeing BGP UPDATE storms in the logs: repeated withdraw/announce for our prefixes.

owen (netops): Quick show output (summary):
```
$ show ip bgp neighbors | include AS64500
Neighbor        AS     MsgRcv  MsgSent  TblVer  Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
203.0.113.2    64500  12000   11850    540     00:04:12  Idle (Admin)
203.0.113.3    64500  12102   11989    541     00:03:48  Active
```
Looks like one session flapping to Idle, other in Active.

dave (oncall): Status check: do we have automatic multi-transit failover in the smart-routing layer? Can we steer traffic off AS64500 quickly?

sam: Yes — we have an online policy to prefer secondary transit (AS64499) for customer-tier routes when packet loss > 15% for 3 consecutive minutes. The smart-router hasn't flipped yet because metrics sampling is noisy. We can force it.

maya: If we force, plan: 1) set localpref higher for announcements via AS64499 2) adjust egress policy at edge for affected prefixes 3) watch for asymmetric path issues.

owen (netops): I'm going to force a temporary localpref reroute for the impacted customer-facing prefixes to prefer AS64499. Command (FRR):
```
route-map PREFER_SECONDARY permit 10
 set local-preference 200
exit
apply map to neighbor 203.0.113.254 out
```
Applying now.

sam: Pushing change through config push. I will gate for 30s and then BGP table check.

(30s later)

sam: Change applied. BGP table shows new best path via AS64499 for the targeted prefixes.

owen (netops): Traffic is shifting. Packet-loss numbers on the secondary transit dropping to baseline. Backend errors for the affected services are reducing.

anna (support): Noted — early customer reports of improvement. Updating the incident status page and sending a heads-up to the affected accounts: "We've detected transient upstream provider routing instability; we've rerouted traffic to secondary transit and are monitoring."

dave (oncall): Good. Open action items: 1) keep monitoring for 30m 2) contact AS64500 support and open a ticket 3) evaluate whether to keep forced localpref for a longer window or revert to automated policy 4) postmortem owner?

owen (netops): Contacted provider NOC via support ticket #AS64500-9876 and opened a phone call. They acknowledge packet loss on their backbone and are investigating a population of routers in their metro region.

maya: Handing off to Owen for 1h watch and further routing work. I'll update dashboards and run a probe sweep across regions to ensure no latent impact.

dave (oncall): Handoff acknowledged — @owen you're primary. I'll stay reachable.

(now at handoff time — metadata: handoff at 1712403000)

owen (netops): Taking over monitoring. Will increase BGP logging to debug-level and keep the forced localpref until provider confirms fix or until we see stable downstream path from AS64500.

sam: Added temporary alert suppressions for noisy withdraw alerts so we don't get thrashed during flaps.

anna (support): Crafting customer-facing message for affected tenants and CS teams.

(20m later)

nowen (netops): Provider reports they've isolated a misconfiguration causing route redistribution loops; they've started to stabilize routers. I'm seeing decreased UPDATE frequency and BGP sessions coming back to Established on their side.

sam: We're seeing normal packet-loss again and error rates dropping to baseline. Propose we gradually remove forced localpref and allow smart-routing to rebalance.

nowen (netops): Rolling back forced localpref in 3...2...1.

(1m)

sam: Rollback complete. BGP tables: best paths split across peers as expected. No immediate regression.

maya: Running post-fix traceroutes — paths look normal. Running extended probes for next 2 hours.

dave (oncall): Great work. Summary for postmortem: upstream transit (AS64500) experienced routing flaps and packet loss due to provider-side redistribution loops. Impact: elevated 5xx and timeouts for hosted API egress in us-east-1 and some Dedicated customers. Mitigation: forced localpref reroute to AS64499, contacted provider NOC, monitored until provider stabilized, rolled back changes. Owner: netops (owen) for next steps with provider and draft postmortem.

anna (support): Notifying impacted customers with timeline + mitigation steps.

nowen (netops): I'll follow up with provider for RCA and request BGP dampening / config fixes on their edge.

dave (oncall): Closing incident in 2 hours if metrics stable. For now, setting status -> monitoring. :white_check_mark:

(Incident thread ends, monitoring ongoing)
